Package com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.application.chat

Interface TurnEvent

All Known Implementing Classes:
TurnEvent.Completed, TurnEvent.Delta, TurnEvent.Error, TurnEvent.Started
public sealed interface TurnEvent permits TurnEvent.Started, TurnEvent.Delta, TurnEvent.Completed, TurnEvent.Error
Typed in-process event emitted by SendMessageUseCase.send(com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.application.chat.SendMessageUseCase.SendMessageCommand) for one chat turn (design §7.1).

The four variants mirror the openapi SSE frame types (started, delta, completed, error). Carrying them as a sealed in-process sum (rather than directly as wire JSON) means:

  • The use case can be tested with StepVerifier without HTTP plumbing.
  • The REST adapter is the single point that translates events to SSE frames (US-11-005).
  • An alternative future transport (WebSocket, gRPC) could plug onto the same Flux<TurnEvent>.

By convention:

  • The first element of a successful turn is exactly one TurnEvent.Started.
  • Zero or more TurnEvent.Delta elements follow.
  • The terminal element on success is exactly one TurnEvent.Completed.
  • On failure, the use case signals Flux.error(java.lang.Throwable) rather than emitting TurnEvent.Error — the REST adapter detects the Reactor error and writes the error SSE frame. TurnEvent.Error exists only for direct wire-translation use cases (e.g. SSE adapters writing a sanitized payload without going through the global exception handler); the use case itself does not emit it.
